source: Book IV printed pp.76-77 = book2-3-4.pdf PDF pp.82-83 (Experiment 5: A Full Adder), image-read; Step 7 speculative derivation from topology
note: Step 7 speculative fixture (derivation A): every expect is derived by hand from the 15 printed wires (programs.json IV-EXP5 wiresEffective, no errata) and the p.77 full-adder rule, not printed. A = slide switch 6 LEFT, B = pushbutton 6 down, carry in = relay 6 held left by hand (relayGrab, contract 1.1; its coil 6E/6F is unwired). Topology: relay 5 coil (through its indicator lamp) is fed from switch 6 set-1 arm 6S, LEFT to 6R=6Z (button N.C.), RIGHT to 6T=6X (button N.O.), so relay 5 = A XOR B; light 6 (sum) hangs on relay 6 set-1 arm 6H, rest to 6J=5G (relay 5 N.O. from 5H plus), held to 6G=5J (relay 5 N.C.), so sum = A XOR B XOR Cin; light 5 (carry) is on 6U=6K, fed by switch 6 set-2 (LEFT: 6V=6T=6X, i.e. A AND B) or by relay 6 set-2 (held: 6L=6J=5G, i.e. Cin AND (A XOR B)). The script runs the printed steps 1-2, then visits all eight input combinations, including the hand letting go of relay 6 at A=1 B=0 (Step 7 notes, IV-EXP5). Asserted: relays 5 and 6, lights 5 and 6, indLamp6 (unwired, always dark) and indLamp5 only while relay 5's coil path is open; a lit indLamp5 shares coil current in series and its class is analog, so it is not asserted. The checkpoint at A=1 B=0 Cin=1 repeats printed step 3 (light 6 OFF, light 5 ON) and adds the relay states. Timing (settle 200 ms, then 100 ms) is a script choice; the page prints none.

script.cite: Book IV printed pp.76-77 = book2-3-4.pdf PDF pp.82-83, Experiment 5 (full adder: relay 6 = carry in, relay 5 = A XOR B, light 6 = sum and light 5 = carry out per step 3 '1 + 0 + 1 = 0 and carry 1'; step 4 'Try other combinations of inputs by moving slide switch 6, pushing pushbutton 6, and/or manually moving relay 6.' prints no outcomes); derived from topology: plus reaches the circuit only at 5H (relay 5 set-1 arm) and 6Y (pushbutton 6 arm); relay 5 coil path 6S-5C-indicator lamp-5E-coil-5F-minus, fed when switch 6 set-1 arm 6S meets 6R=6Z (LEFT, button up) or 6T=6X (RIGHT, button down), so relay 5 = A XOR B; sum lamp 6A-6H: relay 6 at rest 6H-6J=5G (plus only while relay 5 is operated), relay 6 held 6H-6G=5J (plus only while relay 5 is at rest); carry lamp 5A=6U=6K: switch 6 LEFT joins 6U-6V=6T=6X (plus while button down), and relay 6 held joins 6K-6L=6J=5G (plus while relay 5 is operated); relay 6's coil and indicator (6C/6E/6F) are unwired, so relay 6 moves only by hand and indLamp6 never lights; case A=0 B=0 Cin=0: 6S-6T=6X open with the button up, so relay 5 rests; 6J=5G and 6U are dead, so 0 carry 0
script.quote: Relay 6 represents a carry in from a previous stage. Relay 5 represents the sum of inputs A and B; this sum will be added to the carry in to give the sum for the full adder. Notice that a carry signal may come from either of two places: either from the half-adder representing the slide switch and pushbutton (input A and input B), or from the half-adder representing the carry in (relay 6) and the sum of the input (relay 5). Either half-adder can produce a carry signal.
